subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu DM sessions rebuilt after gateway restart — duplicate keys + maintenance pruning

question: What durable Feishu DM policy should OpenClaw adopt for active direct-session retention and malformed or cross-account `open_id` keys?
rationale: The fix changes persisted session identity and retention behavior, so automation cannot safely choose between store growth, history splitting, malformed-key rejection, and doctor repair semantics.

options.title: TTL-aware direct retention plus Feishu repair
options.body: Protect recently active direct sessions from routine maintenance, validate Feishu direct ids at the plugin boundary, and add doctor repair or archive handling for malformed Feishu direct keys.

options.title: Blanket-protect direct sessions
options.body: Treat all human direct sessions as protected maintenance entries, accepting higher long-term store growth while still adding Feishu malformed-key diagnostics separately.

options.title: Keep workaround-only behavior
options.body: Keep `per-account-channel-peer` as the documented workaround and close or defer malformed-key repair until live Feishu proof identifies the truncation source.

recommendation.title: TTL-aware direct retention plus Feishu repair
recommendation.body: Protect recently active direct sessions from routine maintenance, validate Feishu direct ids at the plugin boundary, and add doctor repair or archive handling for malformed Feishu direct keys.

likelyOwner.reason: The core retention policy decision is centered on session maintenance behavior, where this history is strongest.
